clue.text: Wee Sarah gets weary of crossed lines

parts.note: Sal is a short, pet form of the name Sarah, so a little Sarah
to tire is to grow weary

explanation.surface: Little Sarah grows tired of crossed telephone lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee' looks like a description of Sarah's size, but it signals the clipped form of her name.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltire is a diagonal heraldic cross, like St Andrew's on the Scottish flag, made of two crossed bands.

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly or assert
age brings seniority; one's elder has the age advantage

explanation.surface: Someone claims it is unkind to pull rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' reads as unkind, but it is the arithmetic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The mean of a set of numbers is its arithmetic typical value, a synonym in statistics.

clue.text: Hence article about warning to golfers

parts.note: the is the definite article
re means about or concerning
fore is the cry golfers shout to warn of an incoming ball

explanation.surface: A newspaper article follows up on a golf-course warning.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean consequently, a logical connective introducing a conclusion.

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word tenser might be arranged differently, so its letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they are bitter or merely more on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to harbour bitterness and indignation about it.

parts.note: a former gold coin of the realm read as a medicine, punning on a set phrase for a cure-all

explanation.surface: A cynic wonders whether cash solves every problem.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign was a British gold coin worth one pound, so it 'was money'; the set phrase means an infallible cure.
explanation.definitionFit: The fixed phrase denotes a completely effective treatment or panacea.

clue.text: Agree to cheat the poor dog

parts.note: to con is to swindle or cheat
a cur is a worthless mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Someone consents to swindling a wretched mutt.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to share the same opinion, a synonym for assent.

definitions.meaning: to make smaller or reduce in length, as muscles do
a binding deal or legal compact between parties

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to draw together and shrink, and a formal legally binding deal.

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea

indicators.note: maybe hints that the word dear could be arranged otherwise, so its letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: After afternoon tea, someone suggests a party game.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is British slang for tea; 'maybe' rearranges DEAR to RADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Charades is a parlour game of miming words syllable by syllable.

clue.text: Lined up again and made good

definitions.meaning: soldiers dress ranks when they align them, so this is doing it once more
redressing a wrong means remedying or compensating for it

explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-dressed it is aligning troops afresh; as one word it is setting right a grievance.

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Psychiatrists are told to go to a secure spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrinks' reads as psychiatrists, but it is the verb, as in 'peters out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that peters out gradually dwindles and fades away.

parts.note: a guard or watch posted at the front, the leading part of an army

explanation.surface: A fancy timepiece made of lead is shown off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like the metal, but means the front: VAN plus GUARD (watch).
explanation.definitionFit: The vanguard is the foremost division of an advancing force, ahead of the rest.

indicators.note: embraces means one word wraps its arms around another, holding it inside

parts.note: a jack or jack tar is a sailor, as is a tar
Jules Verne, the French novelist

explanation.surface: A sailor hugs a Frenchman named Jules who runs the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a name, but it is a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A taverner is an old word for an innkeeper who keeps a tavern.

parts.note: RE stands for Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A discount offered to an engineering graduate, it is noted.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebate is a partial refund or discount on a sum paid.

definitions.meaning: the general drift or direction of something
a male voice pitched between baritone and alto

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the general drift of an argument and a high male voice part.

clue.text: Those who plough take in little time for exciting relations

indicators.note: take in means the ploughmen admit a short piece into their midst

parts.note: tillers work the soil, ploughing it
hr is the short form of hour

explanation.surface: Farm workers make room for brief, exciting family visits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relations' looks like relatives, but means tellings or narratives.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrillers are suspenseful stories, and a relation is an old word for a narrated account.

clue.text: Peccadilloes of heads of military intelligence

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as MI'S CHIEFS, the bosses of Military Intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Small pranks and petty wrongdoing are mischief; split up, the word gives the chiefs belonging to MI.

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
pounded means battered or beaten

explanation.surface: Someone complains of being arrested and roughed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods or animals seized by authority are put in a pound, so they are seized and held.

clue.text: Creating more stir — in a teacup?

definitions.text: Creating more stir — in a teacup?

indicators.note: creating suggests something new is made from the words more stir, so their letters are reformed

explanation.surface: Someone fusses ever more over a trivial row, a storm in a teacup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creating' rearranges MORE STIR; a storm in a teacup is a fuss over nothing, so the whole clue describes it too.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wilder and more turbulent causes greater commotion, like a bigger squall.

indicators.note: about means the outer word goes round the others

parts.note: to ring is to telephone or call
E for East, oriental meaning eastern
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: A phone call about an Eastern fast proves relaxing.
explanation.definitionFit: Relenting means softening or easing off from a harsh stance.

clue.text: Being tolerant, allowed about nine out

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: let means permitted or allowed

indicators.note: out suggests the word nine is put out of order, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A permissive person let roughly nine people go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like a release of prisoners, but it is the anagram signal; 'Being' is only a link to the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A lenient person is merciful and permissive rather than strict.

parts.note: alludes to the proverb more haste, less pace

explanation.surface: Something is cut back in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'more haste, less speed' says that hurrying reduces it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means rate of movement, which the proverb says haste diminishes.

clue.text: Nice summer-as one might be before north Mediterranean winds

parts.note: ete is French for summer, as spoken in Nice

indicators.note: might be suggests a possible other form of the words, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Summer on the Riviera brings winds from the north across the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective; 'might be' rearranges AS and I.
explanation.definitionFit: The etesians are dry northerly winds blowing across the Aegean each summer.

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: Father is given the role he was promised.
explanation.definitionFit: Parole is a solemn pledge, especially a prisoner's word of honour.

clue.text: One who yearns for something less brief

explanation.definitionFit: Read as long-er it is a person who longs; as a comparative it means more extended.

indicators.note: in means one word sits inside the other

parts.note: eras are periods of time, the times
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Notices of cancelled events are definitely printed in The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Times' looks like the newspaper, but means ERAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasures are deletions where something has been rubbed out or struck off.

parts.note: physical activity good for the body, also a drill or practice routine

explanation.definitionFit: The word means physical activity for fitness and also a practice drill.

clue.text: Appoint head of new radio organization

indicators.note: organization means the letters are arranged into a new order
head of points to the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone names a new chief for the broadcasting body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' gives N from 'new', and 'organization' rearranges it with RADIO.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to appoint someone formally, especially to the priesthood.

clue.text: His likeness by the artist, it's easily caught

definitions.meaning: the person who poses for a portrait painter
in cricket, an easy catch is called this

explanation.definitionFit: A model posing for a portrait, and in cricket a simple catch that should never be dropped.

parts.note: producing a crop, or alternatively surrendering under pressure

explanation.definitionFit: The word means producing, as a field does, and also submitting or giving way.
